source_binding.paper: Four-Coloring P6-Free Graphs. II. Finding an Excellent Precoloring
source_facts: Seeded-precoloring axioms (i)-(v) are exactly connectivity, seed condition, Y0 definition, no mixed-on-Y0-edge condition, and list-size roles.
Legacy 111 permits singleton P={p}, M={m}, N={n} with p in Y(T), n in Y(T'), m in Y0, m complete to p,n, and p nonadjacent n.
Q-admissibility requires endpoint colors f'(p),f'(n) outside f(T) union f(T').
Acceptability violation is a predicate on nonadjacent y,y', unequal lists, and an extension coloring both from the list intersection.

family.name: G_{r,q}
exact_edges: for every a in A_r: a-s, a-z
for every b in B_q: b-t, b-m, b-z

i.proof: G_{r,q} is connected: the fixed base s-t-n-m-p-s is connected; every a attaches to s and every b attaches to t,m; z attaches to all A_r and B_q.

ii.proof: S={s,t} is connected by st. No outside vertex is complete to S: p and every a see s but not t; n and every b see t but not s; m,z see neither.

iii.proof: Exactly m and z have no neighbor in S, so Y0=V\(N(S) union S)={m,z} since X0 is empty.

iv.proof: G[Y0] has no edge because mz is a nonedge, so the mixed-on-an-edge prohibition is vacuous.

v.proof: p and A_r have seed-neighbor color set {1}; n and B_q have {2}, hence all have 3-lists and lie in Y. m,z have no seed neighbor, hence 4-lists and lie in Y0.

false_twin_modules.A_r: independent and all vertices have external neighborhood {s,z}
false_twin_modules.B_q: independent and all vertices have external neighborhood {t,m,z}

lemma.statement: An induced path P_k with k>=4 cannot contain two distinct vertices from one independent false-twin class.
proof: Two false twins are nonadjacent and have identical adjacency to every other selected path vertex.
Hence if both occurred in an induced path, they would have identical open neighborhoods inside that path.
In P_k for k>=4, all vertices have pairwise distinct open neighborhoods: endpoints have distinct singleton neighbors and internal vertices have distinct consecutive-neighbor pairs.

projection_argument: Any induced P7 in G_{r,q} therefore contains at most one A_r vertex and at most one B_q vertex.
Replace a selected A_r vertex by canonical H8 vertex y and a selected B_q vertex by y'.
All adjacencies and nonadjacencies among the seven selected vertices are preserved because the modules are false-twin substitutions.
This would yield an induced P7 in the frozen canonical H8.
The canonical H8 is P7-free by parent authority.
Therefore G_{r,q} is P7-free for every r,q.

proof: The frozen P1 requires a bound g(|S|) independent of n on the full relation or on a canonical pair-superset containing every answer-relevant pair.
Here |S|=2 for all r,q, and every one of the rq distinct pairs is answer-relevant.
Any pair-family containing every answer-relevant pair has size at least rq.
For any proposed finite g(2), choose r,q with rq>g(2).
P1_falsification.scope: Falsifies exactly P1_BOUNDED_PAIR_FAMILY as frozen; no broader complexity claim.

proof: Every answer-relevant pair is an edge of K_{r,q}.
A hitting set U subset A_r, W subset B_q incident with every pair is a vertex cover of K_{r,q}.
If one vertex a is omitted from U and one vertex b is omitted from W, edge ab is uncovered; therefore every vertex cover contains all of one side.
With r=q tending to infinity while |S|=2, no bound g(|S|) is possible.
P2_falsification.scope: Falsifies exactly P2_BOUNDED_VERTEX_HITTING as frozen; does not rule out other repair paradigms.

signature_diagnostic.conclusion: Identical component signatures do not imply bounded survivor-pair multiplicity.

this_family.pair_automorphisms: Sym(A_r) x Sym(B_q) acts transitively on ordered A_r x B_q pairs.
proof_of_projection: For any prescribed gamma,delta in {3,4}, color the selected a_i by gamma and b_j by delta.
Color all other A_r vertices by 3, all other B_q vertices by 4, and z by 1.
Because A_r and B_q are independent and anticomplete to each other, and their fixed neighbors use only colors 1 or 2, this is a proper extension.

P3_diagnostic_not_promotion.interpretation: The family separates multiplicity from representability: pair count and hitting number are unbounded, while this particular family is semantically one pair class.
